# Semiconductor Industry Outlook — Research Evidence Brief

**Task:** task-924bf8fead874d77 — Research semiconductor industry outlook and evidence
**Author:** research | **Date (UTC):** 2026-11-15 | **Run:** run-7a8b646b2a874873
**Scope:** Public, dated evidence for deck sections 4–10 (demand, supply, capex, geopolitics, valuation).
**Status:** Evidence brief. All figures are attributed to the cited source with its as-of date. Gaps and uncertainties are stated explicitly. No figures are invented.

---

## 0. Method & Evidence Limitations (read first)

- **Acquisition window closed** at the fixed stage checkpoint. Only sources actually fetched in this run are cited below. Several planned sources (WSTS.org direct, Semiconductor Intelligence capex page, Infosys outlook) returned fetch errors (redirect loops / stage gate) and are therefore **NOT cited as read** — they are listed in Section 8 as unverified leads only.
- **One primary quantitative source was successfully fetched and read in full:** a June 2, 2026 Bisinfotech article reporting the WSTS Spring 2026 semiconductor market forecast, including the full WSTS forecast table. This is a secondary report of WSTS data; the WSTS primary release itself could not be fetched.
- **Recency note:** The WSTS Spring 2026 forecast (published ~June 2026) is the most recent hard data point obtained. It is ~5 months before the current date (2026-11-15). No Q3/Q4 2026 actuals were obtained. Treat all 2026/2027 figures as forecast, not actuals.
- **No valuation, capex, or geopolitics primary sources were fetched.** Those sections are marked as gaps and must be filled by a follow-up acquisition pass or flagged as unverified in the deck.

---

## 1. Market Size & Growth (VERIFIED — single source)

**Source:** Bisinfotech, "Global Semiconductor Market Surges Beyond USD 1.5 Trillion in 2026 Driven by Extraordinary Memory Expansion," published June 2, 2026. URL: https://www.bisinfotech.com/global-semiconductor-market-surges-beyond-usd-1-5-trillion-in-2026-driven-by-extraordinary-memory-expansion/ (reporting WSTS Spring 2026 forecast).

- Global semiconductor market forecast to grow **~90% in 2026**, reaching **USD 1.51 trillion** (2025: USD 795.6bn; +26.2% in 2025).
- 2027 forecast: **+27%**, reaching **~USD 1.9 trillion** (USD 1,913.7bn).
- Growth is **overwhelmingly memory-driven**.

**WSTS Spring 2026 forecast table (USD millions, YoY %):**

| Segment | 2025 | 2026 | 2027 | 2025 YoY | 2026 YoY | 2027 YoY |

| Americas | 256,476 | 543,654 | 701,439 | 31.4 | 112.0 | 29.0 |
| Europe | 54,694 | 86,643 | 101,587 | 6.7 | 58.4 | 17.2 |

| Asia Pacific | 439,747 | 823,900 | 1,043,326 | 30.3 | 87.4 | 26.6 |
| **Total World** | **795,640** | **1,511,248** | **1,913,683** | **26.2** | **89.9** | **26.6** |
| Discrete | 30,728 | 33,188 | 35,712 | -1.0 | 8.0 | 7.6 |
| Optoelectronics | 43,042 | 44,218 | 46,436 | 4.7 | 2.7 | 5.0 |
| Sensors | 20,894 | 21,516 | 23,002 | 10.4 | 3.0 | 6.9 |
| Integrated Circuits | 700,975 | 1,412,326 | 1,808,533 | 29.9 | 101.5 | 28.1 |
| Analog | 86,519 | 95,358 | 101,662 | 8.7 | 10.2 | 6.6 |
| Micro | 84,867 | 101,655 | 121,966 | 7.9 | 19.8 | 20.0 |
| Logic | 299,547 | 411,371 | 522,820 | 38.8 | 37.3 | 27.1 |
| **Memory** | **230,042** | **803,941** | **1,062,085** | **39.0** | **249.5** | **32.1** |

*Note: figures rounded to whole millions; totals may differ slightly.*

---

## 2. Demand Drivers (PARTIALLY VERIFIED)

- **AI infrastructure / HBM / accelerated computing** is named by the source as "the primary growth catalyst" for the industry. (VERIFIED — same source, June 2, 2026.)
- **Memory** is forecast to grow ~250% YoY in 2026 to >USD 800bn, and a further 32% in 2027 — the single largest swing factor in the forecast. (VERIFIED — same source.)
- **Logic** forecast +37% in 2026, +27% in 2027. (VERIFIED — same source.)
- **Autos, industrial, consumer** demand split: **NOT separately quantified** in the fetched source. The forecast shows only Analog (+10%), Micro (+20%), Discrete (+8%), Sensors (+3%), Optoelectronics (+3%) for 2026 — these are the closest proxies for non-AI end markets and are growing far more slowly than memory/logic. (PARTIAL — inferred from product-category growth, not end-market data.)
- **GAP:** No end-market (auto/industrial/consumer) unit or revenue data obtained. Deck should either omit granular end-market claims or label them as unverified.

---

## 3. Cycle Position & Inventory (GAP — NOT VERIFIED)

- No inventory, book-to-bill, or utilization data was fetched. The WSTS forecast implies a strong upcycle in 2026 driven by memory, but **cycle-position evidence (inventory days, lead times, capacity utilization) is missing**.
- **GAP:** Deck slide 6 (cycle position) cannot be supported by fetched evidence. Recommend either (a) a follow-up acquisition pass, or (b) reframe slide 6 as "what the forecast implies" rather than "where the cycle is."

---

## 4. Structural Themes (PARTIALLY VERIFIED)

- **Memory / HBM:** Strongly supported by the forecast (memory +249.5% in 2026). HBM is named as a demand driver. (VERIFIED — same source.)
- **AI accelerators & advanced packaging:** AI/accelerated computing named as primary catalyst; **no packaging-specific data** fetched. (PARTIAL.)
- **Foundry & node economics:** **NOT VERIFIED.** No foundry revenue, node-mix, or pricing data fetched.
- **Geographic shifts:** Regional forecast shows Americas +112% and Asia Pacific +87.4% in 2026, Europe +58.4%, Japan +27.6%. This is a demand/revenue concentration signal, not a supply-chain-shift signal. (VERIFIED as forecast; interpretation is analytical.)

---

## 5. Supply & Capex (GAP — NOT VERIFIED)

- **No capex data was fetched.** The Semiconductor Intelligence "CapEx Up for Foundry, Memory" page and Infosys outlook both failed to fetch (redirect loop / stage gate).
- **GAP:** Deck slides on capex and supply cannot be supported by fetched evidence. This is a material gap for an investment deck — capex is a key oversupply-risk input.
- **Unverified leads (NOT read, do not cite as evidence):**
  - https://www.semiconductorintelligence.com/capex-up-for-foundry-memory/ (fetch failed: redirect loop)
  - https://www.infosys.com/iki/research/semiconductor-industry-outlook2026.html (fetch blocked by stage gate)
  - https://siliconanalysts.com/market-data/semiconductor-capex (search result only)

---

## 6. Geopolitics & Policy (GAP — NOT VERIFIED)

- **No export-control, tariff, or policy source was fetched.**
- **GAP:** Deck slide 10 (supply chain & policy) cannot be supported by fetched evidence. The regional revenue concentration (Americas +112%) is a weak proxy at best.
- **Unverified leads (NOT read):** none fetched; search results only.

---

## 7. Valuation & Positioning (GAP — NOT VERIFIED)

- **No valuation data (P/E, EV/EBITDA, relative multiples) was fetched.**
- **GAP:** Deck slides 12 (valuation) cannot be supported by fetched evidence. This is a material gap for an investment deck.
- **Unverified leads (NOT read):** none fetched; search results only.

---

## 8. Findings, Uncertainties & Gaps (summary)

**Findings (supported):**
1. WSTS Spring 2026 forecast projects ~90% industry growth in 2026 to USD 1.51tn, driven overwhelmingly by memory (+249.5%). (Source: Bisinfotech/WSTS, June 2, 2026.)
2. 2027 forecast: +27% to ~USD 1.9tn; memory +32%, logic +27%. (Same source.)
3. Regional growth is highly concentrated: Americas +112%, Asia Pacific +87.4% in 2026. (Same source.)
4. Non-AI product categories (analog, micro, discrete, sensors, optoelectronics) grow far more slowly (3–20%), implying a narrow, memory/AI-led upcycle. (Same source.)

**Uncertainties:**
- The forecast is a forecast, not actuals; it is ~5 months old relative to the current date.
- The single fetched source is a secondary report of WSTS data; the primary WSTS release was not read.
- The 90% growth figure is extraordinary and should be stress-tested against a second independent source before being presented as consensus.

**Gaps (material, must be flagged in deck):**
- Capex / supply data — NOT obtained.
- Geopolitics / export controls — NOT obtained.
- Valuation / positioning — NOT obtained.
- Cycle position / inventory — NOT obtained.
- End-market (auto/industrial/consumer) granularity — NOT obtained.

---

## 9. Source List (with as-of dates)

| # | Source | URL | Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bisinfotech — WSTS Spring 2026 forecast report | https://www.bisinfotech.com/global-semiconductor-market-surges-beyond-usd-1-5-trillion-in-2026-driven-by-extraordinary-memory-expansion/ | 2026-06-02 | FETCHED & READ (full) |

- https://www.infosys.com/iki/research/semiconductor-industry-outlook2026.html — stage gate

---

## 10. Handoff Notes

- **Risk (task-c000aa3bd18747f7):** the capex/geopolitics/valuation gaps above are the highest-priority items to fill or explicitly flag as unverified. Do not let the deck present capex or valuation claims as sourced.
- **Marketing (task-f2759b7e1fc14122):** the strongest defensible message is the memory/AI-led concentration of growth and the narrowness of the upcycle. Avoid claims about capex, valuation, or geopolitics that are not in this brief.

## 1. Audience

- **Primary audience:** Internal fund investment team (portfolio managers, analysts, risk officer) at a Hong Kong–based securities investment fund. Presentation is for an internal analytical/decision-support meeting, not a retail client pitch.
- **Secondary use:** May be adapted later for sophisticated advisory clients; that adaptation is OUT OF SCOPE for this deck.
- **Assumed audience knowledge:** Familiar with equity/fixed-income basics, sector rotation, and standard risk terminology. No need to explain what a semiconductor is.
- **Language:** English (internal team working language).

## 2. Purpose & Analytical Focus

- **Purpose:** Provide a forward-looking, evidence-based view of the semiconductor industry from an end-of-2026 perspective, and translate it into actionable investment implications and key risks for the fund.
- **Analytical focus (in scope):**
  1. Industry demand drivers and cycle position as of late 2026 (AI/datacenter, autos, industrial, consumer).
  2. Structural themes: AI accelerators, advanced packaging, memory (HBM), foundry/leading-edge vs mature nodes, geographic supply-chain shifts.
  3. Investment implications: sub-sector attractiveness, valuation/positioning considerations, portfolio construction angles.
  4. Key risks: cyclicality, concentration, geopolitics/export controls, capex oversupply, technology/execution risk, valuation risk.
- **Out of scope:** Single-stock recommendations, options/derivatives strategies, tax/legal advice, non-semiconductor sectors except as context.

## 3. Slide Outline (target ~14–18 slides)

1. Title & purpose
2. Executive summary / key messages (3–5 bullets)
3. Why semiconductors matter to the portfolio (context)
4. Demand drivers: AI & datacenter
5. Demand drivers: autos, industrial, consumer
6. Cycle position & inventory dynamics (as of late 2026)
7. Structural theme: AI accelerators & advanced packaging
8. Structural theme: memory / HBM
9. Structural theme: foundry & node economics
10. Supply chain & geographic shifts / policy

13. Key risks (ranked)

16. Appendix: sources, as-of dates, assumptions

## 4. Key Questions the Deck Must Answer

- Where are we in the semiconductor cycle at end-2026, and what is the evidence?
- Which sub-segments offer the best risk-adjusted exposure for our mandate?
- What could break the thesis (top risks) and how would we detect it early?
- What is priced in, and where is the asymmetry?

- A1: Audience is the internal fund team, not external clients.
- A2: Deck is analytical/decision-support, not a solicitation.
- A3: Base currency context is HKD/USD; fund is a general securities fund (no single-sector mandate).
- A4: "End-of-2026 perspective" means data as of ~Q4 2026; any later data is out of window.
- A5: No proprietary/paid data sources assumed; public sources only.
- A6: Deck length ~14–18 slides; HTML, browser-presentable, slide-by-slide.

- C1: Confirm audience is internal team (vs. external clients).
- C2: Confirm any preferred sub-sector weighting or mandate constraints.
- C3: Confirm whether scenario analysis is desired or should be trimmed.

- Research (task-924bf8fead874d77): gather public, dated evidence for sections 4–10; include source URLs and as-of dates.
- Risk (task-c000aa3bd18747f7): assess and rank risks in section 13; validate scenario plausibility.
- Marketing (task-f2759b7e1fc14122): draft narrative/key messages for slides 2 and 15.

Global Semiconductor Market Surges Beyond USD 1.5 Trillion in 2026 Driven by Extraordinary Memory Expansion

 Vaishali Chauhan

 June 2, 2026
 2 minutes read 

The World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) organization has released its Spring 2026 semiconductor market forecast, significantly raising the industry outlook for both 2026 and 2027.

2026: Semiconductor Market Surpasses USD 1.5 Trillion Driven by Extraordinary Memory Expansion.

Following exceptionally strong results in late 2025 and early 2026, the global semiconductor market is now projected to grow 90 percent in 2026, reaching USD 1.51 trillion. 

The sharp upward acceleration is overwhelmingly driven by the Memory segment, which is forecast to surge by around 250 percent year over year, reaching more than USD 800 billion in 2026. Continued strong demand for AI infrastructure, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and accelerated computing platforms remains the primary growth catalyst for the semiconductor industry. Logic is expected to remain another major contributor, growing 37 percent in 2026. 

Other product categories are forecast to expand at more moderate rates, reflecting a broader industry growth: Microprocessors 20 percent, Analog 10 percent, Discrete Semiconductors 8 percent, Sensors and Optoelectronics with 3 percent.

Regionally, all major markets are projected to show strong growth. The Americas are expected to more than double in 2026 with 112 percent growth, driven by the concentration of AI-related semiconductor demand and cloud infrastructure investments. Asia Pacific is forecast to grow 87 percent, while Europe and Japan are projected to grow 58 percent and 28 percent respectively. 

2027 Outlook: Growth Continues Above Historical Industry Trends 

For 2027, WSTS forecasts the global semiconductor market to grow a further 27 percent, reaching approximately USD 1.9 trillion.

Memory is again expected to lead market expansion with projected growth of 32 percent, while Logic is forecast to increase by 27 percent. Continued deployment of AI systems, advanced computing infrastructure, and expanding semiconductor content across end markets are expected to support ongoing industry momentum. 

All geographic regions are projected to continue growing in 2027, led by the Americas and Asia Pacific.

World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) is an independent, non-profit organization established in 1986 by leading semiconductor manufacturers to provide accurate and reliable market data for the global semiconductor industry. Headquartered in the United States, WSTS serves as the industry’s primary source of monthly semiconductor sales statistics and market forecasts, offering valuable insights into industry trends, regional demand, and long-term growth opportunities.

The organization collects and compiles sales data from a broad range of semiconductor companies worldwide, covering key product categories such as logic devices, memory, microprocessors, analog components, sensors, and discrete semiconductors. Participating companies submit their shipment and sales information confidentially, enabling WSTS to produce comprehensive and trusted market intelligence while protecting individual company data.

One of WSTS’s most important contributions is its regularly published semiconductor market forecasts, which are widely referenced by manufacturers, investors, analysts, governments, and technology organizations. These forecasts provide projections for global semiconductor sales across major geographic regions and product segments, helping industry stakeholders make informed business and investment decisions.

As the only organization that gathers monthly semiconductor sales data directly from a significant portion of the global semiconductor industry, WSTS has become a benchmark source for measuring market performance. Its reports are frequently cited by industry associations, financial institutions, research firms, and media outlets covering the semiconductor sector.

For nearly four decades, WSTS has played a vital role in improving transparency and understanding of the global semiconductor market, supporting strategic planning and fostering greater insight into one of the world’s most important technology industries.

# Semiconductor Industry Outlook — Research Evidence Brief

**Task:** task-924bf8fead874d77 — Research semiconductor industry outlook and evidence
**Author:** research | **Date (UTC):** 2026-11-15 | **Run:** run-7a8b646b2a874873
**Scope:** Public, dated evidence for deck sections 4–10 (demand, supply, capex, geopolitics, valuation).
**Status:** Evidence brief. All figures are attributed to the cited source with its as-of date. Gaps and uncertainties are stated explicitly. No figures are invented.

---

## 0. Method & Evidence Limitations (read first)

- **Acquisition window closed** at the fixed stage checkpoint. Only sources actually fetched in this run are cited below. Several planned sources (WSTS.org direct, Semiconductor Intelligence capex page, Infosys outlook) returned fetch errors (redirect loops / stage gate) and are therefore **NOT cited as read** — they are listed in Section 8 as unverified leads only.
- **One primary quantitative source was successfully fetched and read in full:** a June 2, 2026 Bisinfotech article reporting the WSTS Spring 2026 semiconductor market forecast, including the full WSTS forecast table. This is a secondary report of WSTS data; the WSTS primary release itself could not be fetched.
- **Recency note:** The WSTS Spring 2026 forecast (published ~June 2026) is the most recent hard data point obtained. It is ~5 months before the current date (2026-11-15). No Q3/Q4 2026 actuals were obtained. Treat all 2026/2027 figures as forecast, not actuals.
- **No valuation, capex, or geopolitics primary sources were fetched.** Those sections are marked as gaps and must be filled by a follow-up acquisition pass or flagged as unverified in the deck.

---

## 1. Market Size & Growth (VERIFIED — single source)

**Source:** Bisinfotech, "Global Semiconductor Market Surges Beyond USD 1.5 Trillion in 2026 Driven by Extraordinary Memory Expansion," published June 2, 2026. URL: https://www.bisinfotech.com/global-semiconductor-market-surges-beyond-usd-1-5-trillion-in-2026-driven-by-extraordinary-memory-expansion/ (reporting WSTS Spring 2026 forecast).

- Global semiconductor market forecast to grow **~90% in 2026**, reaching **USD 1.51 trillion** (2025: USD 795.6bn; +26.2% in 2025).
- 2027 forecast: **+27%**, reaching **~USD 1.9 trillion** (USD 1,913.7bn).
- Growth is **overwhelmingly memory-driven**.

**WSTS Spring 2026 forecast table (USD millions, YoY %):**

| Segment | 2025 | 2026 | 2027 | 2025 YoY | 2026 YoY | 2027 YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Americas | 256,476 | 543,654 | 701,439 | 31.4 | 112.0 | 29.0 |
| Europe | 54,694 | 86,643 | 101,587 | 6.7 | 58.4 | 17.2 |
| Japan | 44,723 | 57,050 | 67,332 | -4.3 | 27.6 | 18.0 |
| Asia Pacific | 439,747 | 823,900 | 1,043,326 | 30.3 | 87.4 | 26.6 |
| **Total World** | **795,640** | **1,511,248** | **1,913,683** | **26.2** | **89.9** | **26.6** |
| Discrete | 30,728 | 33,188 | 35,712 | -1.0 | 8.0 | 7.6 |
| Optoelectronics | 43,042 | 44,218 | 46,436 | 4.7 | 2.7 | 5.0 |
| Sensors | 20,894 | 21,516 | 23,002 | 10.4 | 3.0 | 6.9 |
| Integrated Circuits | 700,975 | 1,412,326 | 1,808,533 | 29.9 | 101.5 | 28.1 |
| Analog | 86,519 | 95,358 | 101,662 | 8.7 | 10.2 | 6.6 |
| Micro | 84,867 | 101,655 | 121,966 | 7.9 | 19.8 | 20.0 |
| Logic | 299,547 | 411,371 | 522,820 | 38.8 | 37.3 | 27.1 |
| **Memory** | **230,042** | **803,941** | **1,062,085** | **39.0** | **249.5** | **32.1** |

*Note: figures rounded to whole millions; totals may differ slightly.*

---

## 2. Demand Drivers (PARTIALLY VERIFIED)

- **AI infrastructure / HBM / accelerated computing** is named by the source as "the primary growth catalyst" for the industry. (VERIFIED — same source, June 2, 2026.)
- **Memory** is forecast to grow ~250% YoY in 2026 to >USD 800bn, and a further 32% in 2027 — the single largest swing factor in the forecast. (VERIFIED — same source.)
- **Logic** forecast +37% in 2026, +27% in 2027. (VERIFIED — same source.)
- **Autos, industrial, consumer** demand split: **NOT separately quantified** in the fetched source. The forecast shows only Analog (+10%), Micro (+20%), Discrete (+8%), Sensors (+3%), Optoelectronics (+3%) for 2026 — these are the closest proxies for non-AI end markets and are growing far more slowly than memory/logic. (PARTIAL — inferred from product-category growth, not end-market data.)
- **GAP:** No end-market (auto/industrial/consumer) unit or revenue data obtained. Deck should either omit granular end-market claims or label them as unverified.

---

## 3. Cycle Position & Inventory (GAP — NOT VERIFIED)

- No inventory, book-to-bill, or utilization data was fetched. The WSTS forecast implies a strong upcycle in 2026 driven by memory, but **cycle-position evidence (inventory days, lead times, capacity utilization) is missing**.
- **GAP:** Deck slide 6 (cycle position) cannot be supported by fetched evidence. Recommend either (a) a follow-up acquisition pass, or (b) reframe slide 6 as "what the forecast implies" rather than "where the cycle is."

---

## 4. Structural Themes (PARTIALLY VERIFIED)

- **Memory / HBM:** Strongly supported by the forecast (memory +249.5% in 2026). HBM is named as a demand driver. (VERIFIED — same source.)
- **AI accelerators & advanced packaging:** AI/accelerated computing named as primary catalyst; **no packaging-specific data** fetched. (PARTIAL.)
- **Foundry & node economics:** **NOT VERIFIED.** No foundry revenue, node-mix, or pricing data fetched.
- **Geographic shifts:** Regional forecast shows Americas +112% and Asia Pacific +87.4% in 2026, Europe +58.4%, Japan +27.6%. This is a demand/revenue concentration signal, not a supply-chain-shift signal. (VERIFIED as forecast; interpretation is analytical.)

---

## 5. Supply & Capex (GAP — NOT VERIFIED)

- **No capex data was fetched.** The Semiconductor Intelligence "CapEx Up for Foundry, Memory" page and Infosys outlook both failed to fetch (redirect loop / stage gate).
- **GAP:** Deck slides on capex and supply cannot be supported by fetched evidence. This is a material gap for an investment deck — capex is a key oversupply-risk input.
- **Unverified leads (NOT read, do not cite as evidence):**
  - https://www.semiconductorintelligence.com/capex-up-for-foundry-memory/ (fetch failed: redirect loop)
  - https://www.infosys.com/iki/research/semiconductor-industry-outlook2026.html (fetch blocked by stage gate)
  - https://siliconanalysts.com/market-data/semiconductor-capex (search result only)

---

## 6. Geopolitics & Policy (GAP — NOT VERIFIED)

- **No export-control, tariff, or policy source was fetched.**
- **GAP:** Deck slide 10 (supply chain & policy) cannot be supported by fetched evidence. The regional revenue concentration (Americas +112%) is a weak proxy at best.
- **Unverified leads (NOT read):** none fetched; search results only.

---

## 7. Valuation & Positioning (GAP — NOT VERIFIED)

- **No valuation data (P/E, EV/EBITDA, relative multiples) was fetched.**
- **GAP:** Deck slides 12 (valuation) cannot be supported by fetched evidence. This is a material gap for an investment deck.
- **Unverified leads (NOT read):** none fetched; search results only.

---

## 8. Findings, Uncertainties & Gaps (summary)

**Findings (supported):**
1. WSTS Spring 2026 forecast projects ~90% industry growth in 2026 to USD 1.51tn, driven overwhelmingly by memory (+249.5%). (Source: Bisinfotech/WSTS, June 2, 2026.)
2. 2027 forecast: +27% to ~USD 1.9tn; memory +32%, logic +27%. (Same source.)
3. Regional growth is highly concentrated: Americas +112%, Asia Pacific +87.4% in 2026. (Same source.)
4. Non-AI product categories (analog, micro, discrete, sensors, optoelectronics) grow far more slowly (3–20%), implying a narrow, memory/AI-led upcycle. (Same source.)

**Uncertainties:**
- The forecast is a forecast, not actuals; it is ~5 months old relative to the current date.
- The single fetched source is a secondary report of WSTS data; the primary WSTS release was not read.
- The 90% growth figure is extraordinary and should be stress-tested against a second independent source before being presented as consensus.

**Gaps (material, must be flagged in deck):**
- Capex / supply data — NOT obtained.
- Geopolitics / export controls — NOT obtained.
- Valuation / positioning — NOT obtained.
- Cycle position / inventory — NOT obtained.
- End-market (auto/industrial/consumer) granularity — NOT obtained.

---

## 9. Source List (with as-of dates)

| # | Source | URL | Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bisinfotech — WSTS Spring 2026 forecast report | https://www.bisinfotech.com/global-semiconductor-market-surges-beyond-usd-1-5-trillion-in-2026-driven-by-extraordinary-memory-expansion/ | 2026-06-02 | FETCHED & READ (full) |

**Unverified leads (fetch failed — do NOT cite as evidence):**
- https://www.semiconductorintelligence.com/capex-up-for-foundry-memory/ — redirect loop
- https://www.infosys.com/iki/research/semiconductor-industry-outlook2026.html — stage gate
- https://www.wsts.org/76/Recent-News-Release — redirect loop

---

## 10. Handoff Notes

- **Risk (task-c000aa3bd18747f7):** the capex/geopolitics/valuation gaps above are the highest-priority items to fill or explicitly flag as unverified. Do not let the deck present capex or valuation claims as sourced.
- **Marketing (task-f2759b7e1fc14122):** the strongest defensible message is the memory/AI-led concentration of growth and the narrowness of the upcycle. Avoid claims about capex, valuation, or geopolitics that are not in this brief.
- **Fund manager (task-b0d8941621f54d26):** slides 6, 10, 12 cannot be supported by fetched evidence. Either commission a follow-up acquisition pass or reframe those slides as "open questions / to be verified."
